rationale: Central pydantic BaseSettings configuration object for the backend. It holds environment-derived state (API prefix, secrets, DB URL, SMTP, superuser) and performs only self-validation, so it is a data object. It is used app-wide, which makes it architecturally significant. It configures auth and DB settings but does not itself authenticate or persist anything.

A type interface in TanStack Router's generated routeTree.gen.ts that lists the root's child routes for typing. It is generated boilerplate, not an architectural element. The navigation graph and the routes themselves are modelled from the route definitions, not from this generated typing interface.

FastAPI router module grouping the /utils endpoints (test-email, health-check). It is an API surface grouping of operations under a shared prefix and tag. Authorization is applied via a dependency on superuser rather than being implemented here; email sending is delegated. Moderate significance as a utility route group.

A shadcn/ui-style sidebar primitive. It is a reusable styled button definition in the component library, with props and an asChild slot. It has no callers and is generated-style boilerplate, so its architectural significance is minor, but it does render user interface.

HTTP GET route handler for /users/{user_id}: one method-path API operation contract. It enforces authorization itself (self or superuser, else 403) and reads the User entity from the database session. Authentication is done by the injected CurrentUser dependency, not by this handler.

SQLModel ORM entity (table=True) defining the persisted User record with id, hashed password, timestamps and an owned-items relationship. An ORM model is an object schema in the data-model layer; it maps to the user table. It is a core domain entity, though it holds no authentication logic itself.

A generated API client method bound to POST /api/v1/login/test-token with a bearer security scheme. Per the API layer definition, each generated client method on a distinct method and path is evidence of an Operation. It is generated code, so significance is moderate. It attaches bearer credentials to an HTTP call that validates an access token.

A props type for the DeleteUser React component, holding only an id and a success callback. It is part of the component's signature, an implementation detail rather than an architectural element. The DeleteUser component itself would be modelled in the ux layer.

HTTP route handler for PATCH /me/password, so it is an API operation. It verifies the current password credential and hashes the new one (authentication), then commits the updated user record to the database session (persistence). It is a user-facing endpoint contract rather than an internal helper.

Private config-validation helper that warns or raises when a secret still holds the placeholder 'changethis'. It is a small implementation detail of the Settings class, called only by _enforce_non_default_secrets, and is not an architectural element on its own. It is security-minded config hygiene, not identity verification or access control.

HTTP GET route on the users router that lists users with skip/limit pagination. It is an API operation contract. The handler queries the User table directly through the session, so it does data persistence. In the full-stack template this route is guarded by a superuser dependency at the router level, but that check is not implemented in this symbol.

A trivial TypeScript props interface with a single field for the ItemActionsMenu component. It is boilerplate typing for a UI component, not an architectural element on its own; the component itself would be modelled, not its props type.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts Axios HTTP client runtime. Generic generated boilerplate rather than an application-specific architectural element; it performs HTTP calls to the backend (external integration) but would not be modelled as its own node. The generated API client as a whole might map to the api layer, but this module is just the generic transport scaffolding.

A non-table SQLModel (Pydantic) class used as the response model of the login endpoint. Its shape is published in the OpenAPI schema, so it is an object schema. It only carries the access token and its type and performs no identity verification itself, so no concern flag applies.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts client support module containing URL path/query parameter serialization helpers. Generated boilerplate and formatting utilities sit below the granularity of an architecture element, so no layer applies. It does not itself perform HTTP calls.

A generated SDK client method bound to POST /api/v1/login/access-token. Per the API layer, a generated client method for a distinct method and path is evidence of an Operation. It performs the OAuth2 password-grant token login over HTTP to the backend. As generated code it mirrors the server contract, so significance is moderate.

The root route's layout component in TanStack Router renders HeadContent, the Outlet for child routes, and devtools. Per the spec, a page shell that renders an outlet is modelled as a View. It is thin boilerplate, but it is the app-wide UI shell, so it gets moderate significance.
